Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 1) WHO definition of adverse drug reaction includes a response that is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: ADR is a noxious and unintended response to a drug. It occurs at doses normally used in humans. It is different from poisoning or deliberate overdose.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 2) ADR occurs at doses normally used for prophylaxis, diagnosis, therapy or:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: ADR occurs at normal therapeutic or preventive doses. The WHO definition includes prophylaxis, diagnosis and therapy. It also includes modification of physiological function.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 3) Which is a patient factor influencing ADR?
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Age influences ADR risk. Elderly patients are especially vulnerable. Altered pharmacokinetics and polypharmacy increase risk.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 4) Which comorbidity increases ADR risk by altering drug handling?
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Renal and hepatic disease can alter drug metabolism and excretion. This may increase drug concentration. Toxicity risk becomes higher.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 5) The most common type of ADR is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Type A ADR is the most common type. It is dose-dependent and predictable. It is related to known pharmacological action.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 6) Type A ADR is best described as:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Type A means augmented reaction. It is related to normal pharmacological action. It usually improves with dose reduction.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 7) Insulin-induced hypoglycaemia is an example of:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Insulin lowers blood glucose. Excess pharmacological effect produces hypoglycaemia. So it is predictable and dose-related.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 8) Atropine-induced dry mouth is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors. Dry mouth is related to its known action. So it is a predictable Type A reaction.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 9) Paracetamol-induced hepatotoxicity is commonly classified as:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Paracetamol hepatotoxicity is dose-related. It is predictable with toxic exposure. It is included under augmented reactions.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 10) Antibiotic-induced superinfection is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Antibiotics may disturb normal flora. This can lead to superinfection. It is a predictable pharmacological consequence.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 11) Type B ADR is best described as:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Type B means bizarre reaction. It is uncommon and unpredictable. Allergy, hypersensitivity and idiosyncrasy are included.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 12) Penicillin anaphylaxis is an example of:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Penicillin anaphylaxis is allergic and unpredictable. It is not simply dose-related. So it is classified as Type B.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 13) Idiosyncratic drug reaction belongs mainly to:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Idiosyncrasy is unpredictable. It is not related to usual dose-response action. Therefore it is grouped under Type B ADR.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 14) Type C ADR is mainly due to:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Type C means chronic reaction. It occurs due to long-term drug use. Cumulative toxicity is the key feature.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 15) Isoniazid-induced peripheral neuropathy is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: INH peripheral neuropathy occurs with continued use. It is a chronic cumulative toxicity. Pyridoxine helps reduce this risk.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 16) Analgesic-induced nephropathy is an example of:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Analgesic nephropathy occurs after long-term use. It represents cumulative toxicity. So it is classified as Type C ADR.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 17) Levodopa-induced dyskinesia is classified as:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Dyskinesia with levodopa is related to chronic therapy. It develops with long-term use. It is grouped under Type C ADR.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 18) Type D ADR is characterized by:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Type D means delayed reaction. It appears after a long latency period. Carcinogenesis and teratogenesis are examples.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 19) Carcinogenesis due to drug exposure is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Carcinogenesis appears after a delay. It has long latency. Therefore it is classified as Type D.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 20) Teratogenesis due to drug exposure is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Teratogenic effects may appear after exposure during pregnancy. They are delayed adverse outcomes. So they are grouped under Type D ADR.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 21) Type E ADR is related to:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Type E means ending reaction. It occurs after stopping a drug. Steroid withdrawal is a classic example.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 22) Steroid withdrawal causing adrenal insufficiency is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Steroid withdrawal may cause adrenal insufficiency. It occurs after stopping therapy. Gradual tapering reduces this risk.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 23) In DoTS classification, anaphylaxis with penicillin is an example of dose category at:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Penicillin anaphylaxis can occur even at very low dose. It is not dose-dependent. This is why it is placed under below-therapeutic dose category.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 24) In DoTS classification, nausea with morphine is an example occurring at:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Morphine can cause nausea within therapeutic dose range. It is a known adverse effect. Dose and patient sensitivity influence severity.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 25) In DoTS classification, paracetamol hepatotoxicity is commonly related to:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Paracetamol hepatotoxicity is dose-related. High dose increases toxic metabolite formation. Severe overdose may cause acute liver failure.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 26) In DoTS timing category, penicillin anaphylaxis may occur at:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Penicillin anaphylaxis can occur with first dose in sensitized individuals. It is rapid and unpredictable. Emergency treatment may be needed.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 27) Hyponatraemia with diuretics is classified under DoTS timing as:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Diuretic-induced hyponatraemia often occurs early in treatment. Electrolyte monitoring is important. Elderly patients are more vulnerable.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 28) Benzodiazepine withdrawal syndrome is related to:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Benzodiazepine withdrawal occurs after stopping. Risk increases after prolonged use. Slow tapering reduces withdrawal symptoms.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 29) Clear-cell cancer with diethylstilbestrol exposure is classified as:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Clear-cell cancer after DES exposure appears after a long delay. This is a classic delayed adverse outcome. It fits the timing component of DoTS.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 30) Susceptibility in DoTS classification includes:
Adverse Drug Reaction.option2: Age, allergy, genetics, renal/hepatic disease and adherence
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Susceptibility includes patient-related factors. Age, allergy and genetics may increase ADR risk. Renal/hepatic disease and adherence also matter.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 31) Important drug-related ADR risk factor is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Low therapeutic index drugs have narrow safety margin. Small dose or concentration changes may cause toxicity. Digoxin and cytotoxic drugs are examples.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 32) A prescriber-related factor causing ADR is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: ADR risk increases when monitoring is poor. Prescribers must know drug warnings and patient condition. Monitoring helps detect toxicity early.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 33) Advanced age increases ADR risk mainly due to:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Elderly patients often have reduced renal/hepatic reserve. They may also use multiple drugs. These factors increase ADR risk.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 34) Polypharmacy increases ADR risk because it increases:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Polypharmacy increases chance of drug-drug interactions. It also increases prescribing complexity. ADR risk rises with number of medicines.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 35) Steep dose-response curve increases ADR risk because:
Adverse Drug Reaction.option2: Large dose change is always harmless
Adverse Drug Reaction.option4: Small dose change may cause large effect
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Steep dose-response curve means response changes sharply with dose. Small dose increase can produce toxicity. Careful titration and monitoring are needed.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 36) ACE inhibitors may commonly cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: ACE inhibitors can cause renal impairment and hyperkalaemia. Cough and angioedema may also occur. Renal function and potassium need monitoring.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 37) Antibiotics commonly cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Antibiotics commonly cause GI upset and allergy. Nausea and diarrhoea are frequent. Severe hypersensitivity may occur with some drugs.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 38) Anticoagulants commonly cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Anticoagulants reduce blood clotting. Excess effect causes bleeding. Monitoring is important for drugs like warfarin.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 39) Antipsychotics may commonly cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.option2: Falls, sedation, delirium and extrapyramidal effects
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Antipsychotics can cause CNS and motor adverse effects. Sedation and falls are clinically important. Dopamine blockade may produce extrapyramidal symptoms.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 40) Aspirin and NSAIDs may cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.option2: Gastrotoxicity, GI bleeding and renal impairment
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: NSAIDs can damage gastric mucosa and increase bleeding risk. They may also impair renal function. Risk increases in elderly and renal disease patients.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 41) Benzodiazepines commonly cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Benzodiazepines are sedative drugs. They increase fall risk, especially in elderly. Long-term use may cause dependence.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 42) Beta-blockers commonly cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Beta-blockers reduce heart rate. They may also reduce peripheral circulation sensation. Cold extremities and bradycardia are common adverse effects.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 43) Calcium channel blockers commonly cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Calcium channel blockers can cause ankle oedema. It is due to peripheral vasodilation. It is especially common with dihydropyridines.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 44) Digoxin toxicity commonly includes:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Digoxin toxicity affects GI and cardiac systems. Nausea and anorexia are common. Bradycardia and arrhythmias may be dangerous.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 45) Diuretics commonly cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.option1: Dehydration, electrolyte disturbance, hypotension and renal impairment
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Diuretics increase fluid and electrolyte loss. They can cause hypotension and renal impairment. Electrolyte monitoring is important.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 46) Insulin commonly causes:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Insulin lowers blood glucose. Excess dose, missed meal or exercise can cause hypoglycaemia. It is a predictable Type A adverse effect.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 47) Opioid analgesics commonly cause:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Opioids commonly cause constipation, nausea and sedation. Respiratory depression is the most dangerous acute effect. Tolerance and dependence may occur with chronic use.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 48) A major general risk situation for ADR is:
Adverse Drug Reaction.option1: Single safe drug in young healthy adult only
Adverse Drug Reaction.option3: Polypharmacy with low therapeutic index drugs
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Multiple drugs increase interaction risk. Low therapeutic index drugs have narrow safety margin. The combination greatly increases ADR risk.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 49) Female sex is included as:
Adverse Drug Reaction.option2: A patient factor for some ADRs
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Female sex may increase risk for some ADRs. ADR risk depends on many patient factors. Age, genetics and comorbidity are also important.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 50) Genetic predisposition is mainly a:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Genetic constitution can influence drug response. It may alter metabolism or immune reaction. This can increase susceptibility to ADR.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 51) Altered pharmacokinetics in renal disease is mainly a:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Renal disease changes drug elimination. Drug may accumulate and cause toxicity. Dose adjustment is often needed.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 52) Altered pharmacodynamic response belongs mainly to:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Some patients respond more strongly to usual drug concentrations. Age, organ dysfunction and disease state may alter response. This increases ADR susceptibility.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 53) Poor adherence may contribute to ADR and is classified mainly as:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Poor adherence can cause irregular dosing. It may lead to toxicity or treatment failure. Clear instructions improve safe drug use.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 54) Inadequate knowledge of drug warnings and instructions is mainly a:
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Prescriber knowledge is essential for safe prescribing. Warnings, contraindications and monitoring needs must be considered. Poor prescribing increases ADR risk.

Adverse Drug Reaction.question: 55) Which statement is most accurate?
Adverse Drug Reaction.option1: Type B is common, dose-dependent and predictable
Adverse Drug Reaction.option2: Type E occurs before starting the drug
Adverse Drug Reaction.option3: Type A is rare, dose-independent and unpredictable
Adverse Drug Reaction.option4: Type A is common and predictable; Type B is uncommon and unpredictable
Adverse Drug Reaction.exp: Type A ADR is common, dose-related and predictable. Type B ADR is uncommon, dose-independent and unpredictable. This contrast is one of the most important ADR classifications.
